answer.summary: Pilot data showed that polarization—not coordinated voting rings—was the key problem: the first PageRank-based anti-manipulation approach failed to address bias and could amplify it when one side had more users. That evidence led the team toward a bridging-based algorithm.

sections.heading: What the pilot revealed
sections.content: Baxter said the pilot’s real data made clear that people were polarized. Their first production prototype was a PageRank variant focused on preventing manipulation; it could filter out a ring of users boosting one another, but it did not solve bias and could amplify it if one side had more users. The pilot evidence therefore pointed toward finding agreement across people who typically disagree—the bridging-based approach.
